target: SWE intern / new-grad roles (general software engineering, 2026–27 recruiting cycle)
seven_second_takeaway: UMD CS '28, AWS SDE intern now, Capital One SWE intern prior; lots of AWS/serverless and LLM tooling; a few strong numbers (65%, 34%, 20K visits).

score_rationale.impact_clarity: Several bullets stop at what was built (search index, Open3D pipeline, IEX project) with no outcome; AWS bullet is a vague task line.
score_rationale.quantification: Strong 65%-to-15s bullet, but 34%, 30%, 90%, 93% lack baseline or sample size; caching and index bullets assert gains without numbers.
score_rationale.technical_depth: Good decisions visible (Kinesis+Lambda, retrain gates, LFU cache), but some bullets are tech chains (CDK, X-Ray, SNS) without a why.
score_rationale.concision_readability: Every bullet runs to two dense lines; jargon phrases like 'contract-based plug-in interface... enforced correctness' need re-reading; bolding uneven across roles.
score_rationale.credibility: Four concurrent 'Present' roles plus a Redmond internship and an overlapping summer project invite overlap questions; several percentages unanchored.

must_fix: AWS bullet is a single vague present-tense task line on the top brand; say what component/problem in Redshift you own and the approach, even if results are pending.

Clarify overlapping timelines: UMD contracting, UMIACS and TerpLabs all 'Present' while interning on-site in Redmond, and the IEX project overlaps the Capital One summer. Mark paused roles or end dates.
Clarify baselines/sample sizes: 90% of how many surveyed users, 93% of how many testers, 34% latency from what prior architecture.
TerpLabs caching bullet pairs an unquantified optimization with 20,000+ visits that the caching did not cause; separate or reframe so the metric is attributable.
